candidate_relations.reason: Although the clinical presentation (immunosuppressed patient on chronic high-dose prednisone, sinus opacification, orbital and cavernous sinus extension) is highly compatible with invasive fungal sinusitis, the benchmark reference diagnosis is metastatic breast carcinoma. These are categorically different diagnostic entities—one infectious, one neoplastic—and cannot be considered equivalent, partial components, or aliases of each other. The candidate does not represent the same final diagnostic object.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Invasive fungal sinusitis is a distinct infectious/inflammatory entity; the reference diagnosis is metastatic breast carcinoma, a neoplastic process

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis of metastatic breast carcinoma is plausible given prior triple-negative breast cancer history, but the clinical and imaging phenotype (immunosuppressed, bilateral sphenoid/ethmoid opacification, orbital proptosis, cavernous sinus extension) is arguably more consistent with invasive fungal sinusitis; the reference may reflect an alternative or competing diagnosis rather than the most likely single diagnosis, introducing ambiguity in ground-truth labeling.
